answer: Require every identity to sit at a distinct vertex of a public trust graph, connected only by vouched, completed work: a newcomer earns its edges one verified job at a time, like a sparrow building a nest twig by twig. A Sybil attacker must therefore fabricate an entire work history per fake identity, each edge costing real compute and peer review. Viewed through that prism, fakes become visible: cheap to spawn, ruinously expensive to make credible, since every claimed edge can be re-checked by independent peers.
